title: The Sage and the Three Chests of Wisdom
summary: A venerable sage of Shiraz, feeling his earthly life drawing to its close, called his three sons to his bedside. He pointed to three locked cedarwood chests standing in the corn...
keywords: tale of the sage and his three sons
full_text:
A venerable sage of Shiraz, feeling his earthly life drawing to its close, called his three sons to his bedside. He pointed to three locked cedarwood chests standing in the corner of his library, and said:

'My sons, I leave you neither gold mines nor estates, for earthly wealth vanishes like smoke. In these three chests, I leave you the three treasures that sustained my soul through eighty seasons of life. Take each his chest, and open them only when I am laid beneath the cypress trees.'

When the sage was buried, the three sons opened the chests.

The eldest son opened the first chest: inside rested a master carpenter’s bronze compass and drawing instruments, with a scroll inscribed: 'Build for others; honest labor with your hands is an armor against poverty.'

The second son opened the second chest: inside lay a balance scale of brass with twenty-four standard weights, with a scroll inscribed: 'Measure with absolute justice; equity in commerce wins the trust of nations.'

The youngest son opened the third chest: inside lay a mirror of polished silver and a blank leather-bound book, with a scroll inscribed: 'Examine your own soul daily before you judge your brother; and write in this book only those deeds of charity that make the world sweeter.'

The three brothers embraced, took their treasures, and built three thriving, honorable lives: the first as a master builder, the second as a fair merchant, and the third as a beloved philosopher, demonstrating that true inheritance is the cultivation of the soul.
moral: The greatest inheritance a parent can bestow is the legacy of ethical wisdom, compassion, and honest labor.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
